### Load Samples table

This is the most important input on the analysis, along with the raw data. The *primer_n_samples Table* holds the information of the samples file names, primers, controls, indexes, different projects. **All names under the Unique_file_name colunm must be unique.**

After filling in the table, save it as .csv an place it on the data folder, inside the project's main directory.

-   **Load primers, indexes and samples table.** Reads the configuration CSV containing sample metadata, primers, indexes, and project assignments.

    ```{r}
    primers_n_samples <- readr::read_csv(file = file.path(prjct_path, "data",
                                                          "roots_metabar-primers_n_samples-2026-07-23.csv"))

    # Show if the primer_n_samples table was loaded successfully
    primers_n_samples %>% 
      View()
    ```

-   **Check if file names are really unique.** Validates that Unique_File_name and Sample columns contain no duplicates, stopping execution if found.

    ```{r}
    if (nrow(primers_n_samples) != length(unique(primers_n_samples$Unique_File_name))) {
      message("Your file names are not unique")
      message(paste0("The file names:"))
      message(paste0(primers_n_samples$Unique_File_name[duplicated(primers_n_samples$Unique_File_name)], 
                     collapse = "\n "))
      message(paste0("apear more than once"))

        cat(paste0(primers_n_samples$Sample[duplicated(primers_n_samples$Sample)], 
                   collapse = "\n "))
        message(paste0("apear more than once"))
        } else {
          message("All file names and sample names are unique!")
          }
    ```

## 2. Raw Data Pre-processing

The second phase of the pipeline focuses on the pre-processing and diagnostics of the raw sequencing reads. Before proceeding to ASV inference, it is critical to assess read quality (via FastQC/MultiQC) and validate primer presence and orientation. These diagnostic analyses ensure data integrity and inform the parameters required for the subsequent filtering and cleaning steps.

### Raw data aquisition

-   **Get reads from Base Space.** This part is only required if your read files is on Basespace. If the read files are already downloaded and demultiplexed, place them on the *\$raw_libs* folder and proceed to the next section.

    ```{bash}
    # Navigate to raw files folder 
    cd  /home/gabriel/projetos/mock_pipelines/data/reads/raw;

    # Download run from BaseSpace ----
    # a - autenticate to basespace (must have a basespace account and shared projects/runs)
    bs auth;

    # 2b - list your projects data ----
    bs list datasets;

    # 2c - download multiplexed read files
    for id in $(cat ids.txt); \ do bs download dataset --id $id -o data/reads/raw --extension=fastq.gz; done
    ```

### Preparing multiplexed libraries

`dmx_metabar()` accepts exactly one paired-end multiplexed FASTQ input per execution: one R1 file and one R2 file. A library is therefore defined here as a single raw paired-end dataset associated with one primer.

Each value in the `Lib` column of `primers_n_samples` must contain exactly one value in the `Primer` column. If one physical sequencing run contains multiple primer sets, create separate library entries in `primers_n_samples`, one per primer, and ensure that each entry points to its corresponding raw R1/R2 pair.

If a primer library was sequenced across multiple pools or lanes, concatenate all R1 files in the same order used for the corresponding R2 files. The final concatenated R1 and R2 files must be placed in a library-specific directory containing no other FASTQ files. This is required because `dmx_metabar()` validates that each library directory contains exactly one R1 and one R2 multiplexed FASTQ file.

For example, if ITS2 was sequenced in three pools:

```{bash}
cd /home/gabriel/projetos/roots_metabar/data/reads/raw/multiplexed

mkdir -p ITS2

cat \
  ITS2_pool1_R1.fastq.gz \
  ITS2_pool2_R1.fastq.gz \
  ITS2_pool3_R1.fastq.gz \
  > ITS2/ITS2_combined_R1.fastq.gz

cat \
  ITS2_pool1_R2.fastq.gz \
  ITS2_pool2_R2.fastq.gz \
  ITS2_pool3_R2.fastq.gz \
  > ITS2/ITS2_combined_R2.fastq.gz
```

The same procedure must be repeated independently for every primer library. The paths to these library-specific directories must be recorded in the `Multiplexed data path` column of `primers_n_samples`.

### Demultiplexing

Demultiplexing assigns paired reads to samples according to their forward and reverse index combination. This pipeline uses the custom `dmx_metabar()` function, which calls [Cutadapt](https://cutadapt.readthedocs.io/) to demultiplex paired-end multiplexed FASTQ files.

Each library must contain a single primer and have matching R1 and R2 files. The function identifies the files associated with each library by searching for the library name followed by `_` or `.` in the FASTQ filename. Therefore, library names in the `Lib` column must match the corresponding raw-file names.

[**How `dmx_metabar()` works**]{.underline}

For each library, the function removes leading `N` bases from the forward and reverse index sequences, optionally retains only the first `query_size` bases, and writes separate forward and reverse index FASTA files.

Cutadapt receives the forward-index FASTA through `-g` and the reverse-index FASTA through `-G`. It then generates one paired FASTQ output for every detected forward/reverse index combination. The temporary output files are named using the index names and are subsequently renamed using the corresponding values in `Unique_File_name`.

When `mixed_orientation = TRUE`, the function passes `--revcomp` to Cutadapt. This enables reverse-complement matching and should be used only for libraries in which index orientation may be reversed between read pairs. This can occur when sequencing adapters are inserted into amplicons prepared with a PCR-free library kit. In this situation, approximately half the read pairs carry the forward index on R1 and the other half carry it on R2. The function produces one final R1/R2 pair per sample and does not create separate standard- and flipped-orientation directories.

[**Cutadapt parameters**]{.underline}

-   **`query_size`** (**`--overlap`** and FASTA truncation) — Defines the number of index bases used for assignment. After removal of leading `N` padding, each index sequence is truncated to `query_size` bases before the FASTA files are written. The same value is passed to Cutadapt through `--overlap`, requiring a match across the full query length. Set this value to the actual index length after removing leading `N` bases. Set it to `NA` to use full index sequences and omit the `--overlap` option.

-   **`cut_error_rate`** (**`-e`**) — Maximum error rate allowed during index matching. A value of `0` requires exact matches and is recommended for short, high-quality Illumina indexes.

-   **`cut_indels`** (**`--no-indels`**) — Controls whether insertions and deletions are allowed during matching. When `FALSE`, `--no-indels` is passed to Cutadapt. This is recommended for standard fixed-length indexes.

-   **`cut_pair_filter`** (**`--pair-filter`**) — Defines how paired reads are retained. With `"any"`, a pair is discarded if either read fails to match its expected index. This is the recommended conservative setting for paired-index demultiplexing.

-   **`cut_max_n`** (**`--max-n`**) — Maximum number of `N` bases permitted in each sequencing read. Use `NA` to disable this filter. This option applies to the FASTQ reads, not to the index sequences written to the FASTA files.

-   **`cut_match_wildcards`** (**`--match-read-wildcards`**) — When `TRUE`, ambiguous bases in reads can match IUPAC-compatible bases in the index references. The default is `FALSE`, which is generally preferable for stringent index assignment.

-   **`cut_discard_untrimmed`** (**`--discard-untrimmed`**) — When `TRUE`, read pairs without a valid index assignment are discarded. This is the default behavior and ensures that only reads assigned to known index combinations are retained.

-   **`cut_action`** (**`--action`**) — Defines the treatment of matched index sequences. Use `"retain"` to preserve index sequences for subsequent primer removal, or `"trim"` to remove the matched index sequence during demultiplexing.

[**Outputs**]{.underline}

For each library, `dmx_metabar()` creates the following structure inside `out_path`:

```{text}
<Demultiplexed data path>/
├── indexes/
│   ├── <Primer>--<Lib>--FWD_indexes.fasta
│   └── <Primer>--<Lib>--REV_indexes.fasta
├── temp/
│   └── <Project>/
│       └── <Lib>/
├── log/
│   └── <Project>-<Primer>-<Lib>-<timestamp>.txt
├── plot/
│   └── <Project>-<Lib>_<Primer>-dmx_<timestamp>-plot.pdf
└── cutadapt_output/
    └── <Project>/
        └── <Lib>/
            ├── <Unique_File_name>_R1.fastq.gz
            └── <Unique_File_name>_R2.fastq.gz
```

The final demultiplexed FASTQ files are stored in:

```{text}
<Demultiplexed data path>/cutadapt_output/<Project>/<Lib>/
```

These files are gzip-compressed after Cutadapt completes. The function uses `pigz` when available, using the number of threads specified by `gz_threads`; otherwise, it falls back to single-threaded `gzip`.

The `log/` directory contains the complete Cutadapt output for each processed library. Inspect this file if Cutadapt fails or if the demultiplexing rate is unexpectedly low.

The function also reports the total size and number of raw and demultiplexed read pairs, together with their retention percentages. A PDF bar plot is saved in `plot/`, showing the number of demultiplexed read pairs for each sample. Samples with no output FASTQ files are retained in the plot with zero reads.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

-   **Validate the library-to-primer relationship.** Necessary step before running the demultiplex.

    ```{r}
    library_primer_check <- primers_n_samples %>%
      dplyr::distinct(Lib, Primer) %>%
      dplyr::count(Lib, name = "n_primers")

    invalid_libraries <- library_primer_check %>%
      dplyr::filter(n_primers != 1)

    if (nrow(invalid_libraries) > 0) {
      stop(
    "Each Lib must contain exactly one Primer. Invalid Lib values: ",
    paste(invalid_libraries$Lib, collapse = ", "),
    ". Split the affected libraries in primers_n_samples before demultiplexing."
      )
    }

    # Define wich libraries will be demultiplexed
    all_Libs <- primers_n_samples %>%
      dplyr::pull(Lib) %>%
      unique()

    # all_Libs <- all_Libs[1]

    print(all_Libs)
    ```

-   **Run demultiplex function.** Iterates over libraries in the configuration table (`primers_n_samples`) and applies the custom `dmx_metabar2` function to split samples using the index information.

    ```{r}
    # Loop over projects and run demultiplexing
    for (LIB in all_Libs) {
      
      # Filter data for current project
      LIB_data <- primers_n_samples %>% dplyr::filter(Lib == LIB)
      
      # Extract directories (using unique to get the single value for this project)
      raw_dir <- BiocGenerics::unique(LIB_data$`Multiplexed data path`)
      out_dir <- BiocGenerics::unique(LIB_data$`Demultiplexed data path`)
      
      # Run demultiplexing
      tictoc::tic(paste0("Demultiplexing raw data"))
      
      dmx_metabar(multiplex_file_R1 = list.files(raw_dir, 
                                                 pattern = "_R1.*\\.fastq(\\.gz)?$",
                                                 full.names = TRUE),
                  multiplex_file_R2 = list.files(raw_dir, 
                                                 pattern = "_R2.*\\.fastq(\\.gz)?$",
                                                 full.names = TRUE),
                  out_path = out_dir,
                  project = paste0(BiocGenerics::unique(LIB_data$Project), 
                                   collapse = "-"),
                  Unique_File_name = LIB_data$Unique_File_name,
                  primers = LIB_data$Primer,
                  libs = LIB_data$Lib,
                  samples_names = LIB_data$Sample,
                  FWD_sequence = LIB_data$`Full sequence FWD`,
                  idxs_FWD_names = LIB_data$`Index name FWD`,
                  REV_sequence = LIB_data$`Full sequence REV`,
                  idxs_REV_names = LIB_data$`Index name REV`,
                  cut_threads = 60, # Number of threads
                  mixed_orientation = TRUE, # Dual-mixed Library
                  query_size = 20, # Matching size of 46.97%
                  # query_size = 12, # Matching of 50.64%
                  # query_size = 8, # Matching of 52.63%
                  cut_error_rate = 0, # Exact match with the tags provided
                  cut_indels = FALSE, # No indels
                  cut_pair_filter = "any",# Discart the pair if ANY read does not have tag
                  cut_max_n = 0, # Discart the pair if one of reads contains N bases
                  cut_action = "retain" # Retain the tags for the downstream Primer Removal
      )
      tictoc::toc()
    }
    ```

### Quality checking

The raw sequencing reads are assessed for overall quality before any processing steps. This step runs FastQC and MultiQC on the demultiplexed files, generating per-project interactive reports. The resulting quality profiles — particularly per-position quality scores, GC content, and read length distributions — provide the baseline needed to interpret subsequent primer detection and filtering results.

-   **Validate demultiplexed outputs.** Read the sample audit files immediately after demultiplexing. The pipeline stops if a sample has an incomplete output pair or if file organization failed.

    ```{r}
    read_files <- primers_n_samples %>%
      dplyr::rowwise() %>%
      dplyr::mutate(Read_file = list(list.files(
        path = file.path(`Demultiplexed data path`, "cutadapt_output", Project),
        pattern = paste0(Unique_File_name, "_R.*\\.fastq\\.gz$"),
        recursive = TRUE,
        full.names = TRUE))) %>%
      dplyr::pull(Read_file) %>%
      unlist() %>%
      unique()

    # 1. Obtain the size of the demultiplexed files
    file_sizes <- file.info(read_files)$size

    # 2. Filter only the files with real data (bigger than 100 bytes)
    valid_read_files <- read_files[file_sizes > 100]

    # Identify which files are exactly the empty ones
    empty_files <- setdiff(read_files, valid_read_files)

    # 3. Calculate how many were empty
    empty_count <- length(empty_files)

    # 4. Logical verification and messages
    if (length(valid_read_files) > 0) {
      message(length(valid_read_files), " read files with actual data found for QC.")
      
      if (empty_count > 0) {
        message("Notice: ", empty_count, " empty files (0 reads) were detected and ignored:\n", 
                paste(basename(empty_files), collapse = "\n"))
      }
      
      # Obtain the read_files variable with only the valid files with reads
      read_files <- valid_read_files
      
    } else {
      stop("Files were found, but ALL of them are empty (0 reads). Check your demultiplexing step or `Demultiplexed data path`.")
    }
    ```

-   **Run FastQC and MultiQC by project.** Creates per‑project folders and runs quality control in batch using system calls.

    ```{r}
    for (PRJ in all_projects) {
      
      # Create output directories
      fastqc_path <- file.path(qual_path, PRJ, "fastqc")
      multiqc_path <- file.path(qual_path, PRJ, "multiqc")
      
      dir.create(fastqc_path, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
      dir.create(multiqc_path, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
      
      # Filter reads per project
      raw_path <- primers_n_samples$`Demultiplexed data path`[primers_n_samples$Project == PRJ] %>%
        unique()
      
      project_reads <- read_files[stringr::str_detect(read_files, paste0(raw_path, collapse = "|"))]
      
      # Avoid ARG_MAX limit by using a temporary file list for GNU parallel
      tmp_list <- tempfile(fileext = ".txt")
      writeLines(project_reads, tmp_list)
      
      # 1. Run FastQC
      cmd_fastqc <- paste0("parallel fastqc {} -t 20 -o ", fastqc_path, " < ", tmp_list)
      system(cmd_fastqc)
      
      # Clean up temporary file
      unlink(tmp_list)
      
      # 2. Run MultiQC
      report_name <- paste0(PRJ, "--sequencing_quality-MultiQC_report.html")
      cmd_multiqc <- paste0("multiqc --no-data-dir --interactive ", fastqc_path,
                            " --filename ", file.path(multiqc_path, report_name))
      system(cmd_multiqc)
      
      # 3. Open report
      browseURL(file.path(multiqc_path, report_name))
    }
    ```

### Primer detection Analysis

The following workflow performs a critical diagnostic check on the raw sequencing reads before any actual sequence trimming or filtering takes place. In this section, the script intentionally searches for all defined primer sequences across all samples, evaluating four different sequence orientations (`Forward`, `Complement`, `Reverse`, and `RevComp`\[Reverse-Complement\]). This comprehensive "all-versus-all" screening serves three primary quality control purposes:

1.  It validates that the expected primers are successfully detected within their corresponding samples;

2.  It checks for potential laboratory cross-contamination or sequencing index-hopping by ensuring samples do not harbor unexpected primer sets;

3.  It diagnoses the library's structural geometry (e.g., standard vs. mixed orientation) and highlights the presence of read-through events in short amplicons. Ultimately, this step generates a detailed visual matrix, allowing users to verify the integrity, purity, and orientation of the sequencing run before deploying Cutadapt for the actual primer excision.

#### Identify paired-end read files

-   **List R1/R2 files.** Scans the raw data directory for FASTQ files matching common Illumina naming patterns for forward and reverse reads.

    ```{r}
    # Base directory of the read files (assumes all reads share the same root as the first file)
    data_dir <- dirname(read_files) %>% 
      unique()

    # List all forward (R1) FASTQ files using common naming patterns
    R1_pattern <- "_R1_001.fastq|_R1_001.fastq.gz|\\.1.fastq|\\.R1.fastq|R1.fq|R1.fastq|1.fq.gz|-R1.fastq.gz"

    all_fnFs <- list.files(data_dir, 
                           pattern = R1_pattern,
                           full.names = TRUE) %>%
      sort()

    # List all reverse (R2) FASTQ files using common naming patterns
    R2_pattern <- "_R2_001.fastq|_R2_001.fastq.gz|\\.2.fastq|\\.R2.fastq|R2.fq|R2.fastq|2.fq.gz|-R2.fastq.gz"

    all_fnRs <- list.files(data_dir, 
                           pattern = R2_pattern,
                           full.names = TRUE) %>%
      sort()

    # Final verification message
    n_R1 <- length(all_fnFs)
    n_R2 <- length(all_fnRs)

    if (n_R1 == n_R2 && n_R1 > 0) {
      # Message for successful match
      msg_body <- paste0("✓ Paired: ", n_R1, " R1 files match exactly the ", n_R2, " R2 files.")
      
      if (n_R1 <= 100) {
        msg_body <- paste0(msg_body, "\n\nVerify if all expected pairs are listed:\n\nR1 files:\n",
                           paste0("  ", basename(all_fnFs), collapse = "\n"),
                           "\n\nR2 files:\n",
                           paste0("  ", basename(all_fnRs), collapse = "\n"))
        } else {
          msg_body <- paste0(msg_body, "\n\n(Skipping detailed file list due to large number of files: ",
                             n_R1, " in total)")
          }
      message(msg_body)
      
      } else {
        # Message for mismatch
        msg_body <- paste0("✗ MISMATCH: ", n_R1, " R1 files vs ", n_R2, " R2 files.")
        
        # Even on mismatch, we only list if the number is manageable
        if (n_R1 <= 100 && n_R2 <= 100) {
          msg_body <- paste0(msg_body, "\nR1 files:\n", paste0("  ", basename(all_fnFs), collapse = "\n"),
                             "\n\nR2 files:\n", paste0("  ", basename(all_fnRs), collapse = "\n"))
          }
        message(msg_body, "\nCheck if file names in `primers_n_samples` match actual FASTQ files on disk.")
      }
    ```

-   **Match files to samples.** Associates each sample in primers_n_samples with its corresponding R1/R2 files by matching directory path and Unique_File_name.

    ```{r}
    sample_idx_tbl_wide <- primers_n_samples %>%
      dplyr::select("Unique_File_name", "Lib", "Run", "Project",
                    "Researcher", "Sample", "Primer", "Type",
                    "Demultiplexed data path", dplyr::ends_with("ontrol")) %>%
      dplyr::rowwise() %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        # R1 file search
        FWD_R1 = {
          base_path <- file.path(`Demultiplexed data path`, "cutadapt_output", Project)
          files <- list.files(
            path = base_path,
            pattern = paste0(Unique_File_name, "_R1.*\\.fastq\\.gz$"),
            recursive = TRUE,
            full.names = TRUE
          )
          if (length(files) > 1) {
            warning(sprintf("Multiple R1 files found for %s: %s", 
                           Unique_File_name, paste(files, collapse = ", ")))
          }
          if (length(files) > 0) files[1] else NA_character_
        },
        # R2 file search
        FWD_R2 = {
          base_path <- file.path(`Demultiplexed data path`, "cutadapt_output", Project)
          files <- list.files(
            path = base_path,
            pattern = paste0(Unique_File_name, "_R2.*\\.fastq\\.gz$"),
            recursive = TRUE,
            full.names = TRUE
          )
          if (length(files) > 1) {
            warning(sprintf("Multiple R2 files found for %s: %s", 
                           Unique_File_name, paste(files, collapse = ", ")))
          }
          if (length(files) > 0) files[1] else NA_character_
        }
      ) %>%
      dplyr::ungroup()

    # Show table
    View(sample_idx_tbl_wide)
    ```

-   **Build long-format file table.** Adds paths for future paired-output files and reshapes the table to long format, with one row per file per stage.

    ```{r}
        # Create paths for the future paired-output files and reshape to long format
    sample_idx_tbl <- sample_idx_tbl_wide %>%
      dplyr::mutate(FWD_R1_paired = file.path(paired_libs,
                                              paste0(Unique_File_name, 
                                                     "--FWD_R1_paired.fastq.gz")),
                    FWD_R2_paired = file.path(paired_libs,
                                              paste0(Unique_File_name, 
                                                     "--FWD_R2_paired.fastq.gz"))) %>%
      tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = c(FWD_R1, FWD_R2, FWD_R1_paired, FWD_R2_paired),
                          names_to  = "Stage",
                          values_to = "Read file") %>%
      dplyr::mutate(Unique_File_name_Primer = Unique_File_name)

    # Show table
    View(sample_idx_tbl)
    ```

#### Generate primer database

-   **Generate IUPAC codes function.** Converts IUPAC ambiguity codes into regular expressions, enabling the direct search of degenerate primers on raw sequencing reads.

    ```{r}
    # Convert IUPAC codes to regex. Enables searching degenerate primers directly on reads.
    iupac2seq <- function(dna_seq) {
      iupac_code <- c("A" = "A", "C" = "C", "G" = "G", "T" = "T",
                      "Y" = "[CT]", "R" = "[AG]", "H" = "[ACT]", "M" = "[AC]",
                      "K" = "[GT]", "S" = "[GC]", "W" = "[AT]", "B" = "[CGT]",
                      "D" = "[AGT]", "V" = "[ACG]", "N" = "[ACGT]")
      stringr::str_replace_all(dna_seq, iupac_code)
      }
    ```

-   **Primer database.** Defines primer names and sequences (including IUPAC codes where applicable). Comments are retained only where they document the biological identity of the primers.

    ```{r}
    # Obtain primers sequences from primers_n_samples
    all_primers <- primers_n_samples %>%
      distinct(Primer, `Primer sequence FWD`, `Primer sequence REV`) %>%
      pivot_longer(-Primer, names_to = "direction", values_to = "sequence") %>%
      mutate(name = paste0(Primer, "_", ifelse(direction == "Primer sequence FWD", "FWD", "REV"))) %>%
      select(name, sequence) %>%
      deframe()
      
    # OPTIONAL: Define vector of active primers (uncomment lines to activate specific primer pairs)
    {
      # all_primers <-
      # c(
        # NeoFish_FWD = "CGCCGTCGCAAGCTTACCCT",
        # NeoFish_REV = "AGTGACGGGCGGTGTGTGC",
        # MiFish_FWD = "GTCGGTAAAACTCGTGCCAGC",
        # MiFish_REV = "ACATAGTGGGGTATCTAATCCCAGTTTG"
        # MiBird__FWD = "GGGTTGGTAAATCTTGTGCCAGC",
        # MiBird__REV = "CATAGTGGGGTATCTAATCCCAGTTTG",
        # MiFish variants (12S, fishes)
        # MiFishEM__FWD  = "GTCGGTAAAACTCGTGCCAGC", 
        # MiFishEMs__FWD = "GTCGGTAAAACTCGTGCCAGC",
        # MiFish__FWD    = "AAACTCGTGCCAGC",       
        # MiFish2__REV   = "CATAGTGGGGTATCTAATCCCAGTTTG",
        # MiFishEMs__REV = "CATAGTGGGGTATCTAATCCCAGTT",
        # MiFishEM__REV  = "CATAGTGGGGTATCTAATCCCAGTTTG",
        # MiFish__REV    = "TCTAATCCCAGTTTG",
        # p12SV5__FWD = "TTAGATACCCCACTATGC",
        # p12SV5__REV = "TAGAACAGGCTCCTCTAG",
        # V12Su__FWD = "GTGCCAGCNRCCGCGGTYANAC",
        # V12Su__REV = "ATATRGGGTATCTAATCCYAGT",
        # V16Su__FWD = "ACGAGAAGACCCYRYGRARCTT",
        # V16Su__REV = "TCTHRRANAGGATTGCGCTGTTA",
        # VCOIu__FWD = "CAYGCHTTTGTGNATRATYYTYTT",
        # VCOIu__REV = "GGRGGRTADACDGTYCANCCNGT"
        # (Other primer pairs can be re‑added here following the same pattern)
        # ) %>% 
      # stats::na.omit()
      }

    # Convert primer vector to list of single-row tibbles (for allOrients function)
    primers_list <- tibble::tibble(`Primer seq`  = all_primers,
                                   `Primer name` = names(all_primers)) %>%
      split(1:nrow(.))

    # Print primers
    primers_list
      
    # Create reference table with IUPAC → Regex conversion for inspection
    all_primers_tbl <- tibble::tibble(Primer = names(all_primers),
                                      `IUPAC sequence` = all_primers) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(`Regex sequence` = iupac2seq(`IUPAC sequence`))

    # Show primers
    all_primers_tbl
    ```

#### Generate all primers orientations

-   **All primer orientations function.** The function `allOrients` creates forward, reverse, complement, and reverse-complement variants for each primer using Biostrings, organizing them into a tidy table with orientation labels, parsed IUPAC sequences, and standardized naming for robust downstream read matching.

    ```{r}
    # Generates all 4 orientations (FWD/REV/COMP/REVCOMP) for a single primer
    allOrients <- function(primers_list) {
      require(Biostrings)
      
      dna <- Biostrings::DNAString(primers_list$`Primer seq`)
      
      orients <- c(Forward= dna,Complement = Biostrings::complement(dna),
                   Reverse = Biostrings::reverse(dna),
                   RevComp = Biostrings::reverseComplement(dna))
      
      primer_tbl <- sapply(orients, toString)
      
      primer_tbl <- tibble::tibble(Sequence = primer_tbl,
                                   `Primer orientation` = names(primer_tbl)) %>%
        dplyr::mutate(Primer = primers_list$`Primer name`) %>%
        tidyr::unite(col = "Orientation name",
                     Primer,
                     `Primer orientation`,
                     remove = FALSE) %>%
        dplyr::mutate(`Primer pair` = stringr::str_remove_all(Primer,
                                                              "_FWD$|_REV$"),
                      `Parsed sequence` = iupac2seq(Sequence))
      
      base::names(primer_tbl$Sequence) <- primer_tbl$`Orientation name`
      
      primer_tbl
      }
    ```

-   **Generate all primer orientations** Produces all orientations (`Forward`/`Reverse`/`Complement`/`RevComp`) and their regex representation for downstream searching.

    ```{r}
    # Apply all Orients to all primers and clean final table
    primers_all_orients <- purrr::map_dfr(primers_list, 
                                          allOrients) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(`Primer pair` = stringr::str_remove_all(Primer, "_FWD$|_REV$"))

    # Inspect primers orientations
    View(primers_all_orients)
    ```

#### Per-file primer hits

-   **Define primer counting function.** The function `multi_primerHits()` applies B. Callahan's `primerHits()` function across all primer orientations for a single FASTQ file, returning a table of hit counts per orientation. Defining it here keeps the primer-counting logic close to where it is used.

    ```{r}
    # Counts how many reads in a FASTQ file contain a given primer
    primerHits <- function(primer, file_name) {
      
      nhits <- Biostrings::vcountPattern(primer,
                                         ShortRead::sread(ShortRead::readFastq(file_name)),
                                         fixed = FALSE,
                                         max.mismatch = 1)
      sum(nhits > 0)
      }

    # primerHits function applied to all primers orientations
    multi_primerHits <- function(Read_file, primers, Unique_File_name) {
      
      primer_counts <- purrr::map_df(primers,
                                     .f = primerHits,
                                     file_name = Read_file)
      
      primer_counts %>% dplyr::mutate(`Read file` = Read_file,
                                      Unique_File_name = Unique_File_name)
      }
    ```

-   **Per‑file primer hits.** Counts the number of reads that contain a given primer pattern (with up to 1 mismatch). All four orientations generated by `allOrients()` — `Forward`, `Complement`, `Reverse`, and `RevComp` — are searched simultaneously against each R1 and R2 file, enabling detection of primers regardless of read orientation or library preparation strategy. The resulting table is then joined with sample metadata and annotated with total read counts per file to allow proportional comparisons across samples.

    ```{r}
    # Select only raw reads (R1/R2) for primer detection
    reads_seqs_tbl <- sample_idx_tbl %>%
      dplyr::filter(Stage %in% c("FWD_R1", "FWD_R2")) %>%
      dplyr::select(`Read file`, Unique_File_name, Stage,
                    Project, Run, Primer)

    # Create named vector of FASTQ paths (names = sample identifiers)
    reads_seqs <- reads_seqs_tbl$`Read file`
    names(reads_seqs) <- reads_seqs_tbl$Unique_File_name

    # Extract all primer orientations as named vector for counting
    primers_seqs <- primers_all_orients %>%
      dplyr::pull(Sequence, name = `Orientation name`)

    # Set up parallel processing (all cores minus 2)
    # cores_to_use <- future::availableCores() - 2
    cores_to_use <- 60
    future::plan(future::multisession(workers = cores_to_use))
      
    # Count primer occurrences across all files x all primer orientations (parallel)
    {
      tictoc::tic("Counting primers")
      
      message("Searching primers across ", length(reads_seqs), " files using ",
              cores_to_use, " cores. This may take a few minutes...")
      
      primers_in_Nreads <- furrr::future_imap_dfr(reads_seqs,
                                                  .f = function(val, nm) {
                                                    multi_primerHits(Read_file = val,
                                                                     Unique_File_name = nm,
                                                                     primers = primers_seqs)
                                                    },
                                                  .options = furrr::furrr_options(seed = NULL))
      
      tictoc::toc()
      
      message("✓ Primer search complete. Results in `primers_in_Nreads`:\n",
            "  ", length(unique(primers_in_Nreads$Unique_File_name)), " samples × ",
            length(primers_seqs), " primer orientations across ",
            length(reads_seqs), " files.")
    }

    # Join with sample metadata and calculate total reads per file
    primers_in_Nreads <- primers_in_Nreads %>%
      select(-c(Unique_File_name)) %>% 
      dplyr::left_join(sample_idx_tbl, 
                       by = "Read file") %>%
      dplyr::mutate(Read = dplyr::if_else(stringr::str_detect(Stage, "R1"), 
                                          "R1", "R2")) %>%
      tidyr::unite(col = "Unique_File_name_Read",
                   Unique_File_name,
                   Read,
                   sep = " ",
                   remove = FALSE) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(`Total reads` = ShortRead::countFastq(dirPath = `Read file`)[, 1])

    View(primers_in_Nreads)
    ```

#### Primers identified in each sample

-   **Prepare data.** Transform the primer hits table into a long format suitable for visualization with `ggplot2`. This step filters out unobserved primers and organizes metadata.

    ```{r}
    # Prepare primer counts for plots in ggplot

    # Check available orientation names (for debugging)
    # primers_all_orients$`Orientation name`

    # Print column names formatted for selection (helper for coding)
    # primers_in_Nreads %>% colnames() %>% paste0(collapse = '",\n') %>% cat()

    # Convert primer hits table to long format
    primers_in_Nreads_long <- primers_in_Nreads %>% 
      dplyr::select(!dplyr::ends_with(c("_Complement", "_Reverse"))) %>% 
      tidyr::gather(key = Sequences,
                    value = Count,
                    ends_with("FWD_Forward"),
                    ends_with("FWD_RevComp"),
                    ends_with("REV_Forward"),
                    ends_with("REV_RevComp")) %>% 
      dplyr::mutate(Sequences = as.factor(Sequences),
                    Sample = factor(Sample,
                                    levels = sample_levels)) %>% 
      dplyr::select(-c("Read file")) %>% 
      # Remove columns that are entirely NA
      dplyr::select(where(function(x) any(!is.na(x)))) %>% 
      # Filter out primers with zero counts
      dplyr::filter(Count != 0)

    #View table
    View(primers_in_Nreads_long)
    ```

-   **Configure plot settings.** Load necessary visualization libraries and define the factor levels for sample ordering in the plots.

    ```{r}
     # Plot identified primers
    primer_colours <- c("purple", "red", "yellow",
                        "green", "dark green")

    # Create levels for Files display on plot based on the prepared data
    Unique_File_name_Read_levels <- primers_in_Nreads_long %>% 
      dplyr::pull(Unique_File_name_Read) %>% 
      base::unique()
    ```

-   **Generate diagnostic plot.** Iterate through each project to create specific primer abundance plots. The loop filters data per project, generates a tile/bar plot showing primer presence and proportion, and saves the output as a PDF.

    ```{r}
    # Loop through all projects defined in the workflow
    for (PRJ in all_projects) {
      
      options(scipen = 10000)

      # 1. Filter and prepare data ONCE for the current project
      # This avoids filtering the large dataset multiple times inside the loop
      project_data <- primers_in_Nreads_long %>%
        dplyr::filter(Project == PRJ) %>%
        dplyr::mutate(
          
          # Pre-format labels and calculate percentages to keep ggplot clean
          Sequences_lbl = stringr::str_replace_all(Sequences, "__|_", "\n"),
          Primer_lbl    = stringr::str_replace_all(Primer, ";", "\n"),
          Pct_Reads     = (Count / `Total reads` * 100))
      
      # 2. Calculate dynamic dimensions based on actual data
      n_samples <- length(unique(project_data$Unique_File_name_Read))
      n_primers <- length(unique(project_data$Primer))

      # 3. Create the plot object
      primers_tile <- project_data %>%
        ggplot2::ggplot(aes(y = Unique_File_name_Read)) +
        # Bar layer
        ggplot2::geom_bar(aes(x = `Total reads`,
                              fill = Pct_Reads,
                              # color = Primer,
                              group = Sequences),
                          stat = "identity",
                          position = "dodge",
                          linewidth = 0.05,
                          linetype = 2,
                          alpha = 0.5) +
        # Text labels for counts
        ggplot2::geom_text(aes(x = `Total reads`, 
                               label = Count),
                           hjust = -0.1, 
                           size = 3.5) +
        # Color scales
        ggplot2::scale_fill_gradientn(name = "Proportion of reads\nwith primer (%)",
                                      colours = primer_colours,
                                      values = c(0, 1),
                                      na.value = "white") +
        # Axes and Guides
        ggplot2::scale_y_discrete(limits = rev) +
        ggplot2::scale_x_log10(
          breaks = c(10, 100, 1000, 10000, 100000),
          expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.4))) +
        ggplot2::scale_alpha(guide = 'none') +
        ggplot2::guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(fill = "white", 
                                                                 size = 10))) +
        
        # Theme adjustments
        ggplot2::theme_light(base_line_size = 0.025, base_size = 10) +
        ggplot2::theme(axis.title.x = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
                       axis.title.y = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
                       axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 9),
                       axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9),
                       strip.text.x = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold"),
                       strip.text.y = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold"),
                       plot.title = element_text(size = 16.5, face = "bold"),
                       panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "darkgrey", linewidth = 0.2),
                       panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank(), 
                       plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10.5),
                       legend.text = element_text(size = 9),
                       legend.title = element_text(size = 10.5, face = "bold")) +
        
        # Dynamic horizontal lines based on actual sample count
        # ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = seq(0.5, n_samples + 0.5, 2), 
        #                     color = "darkgrey") +
        
        # Titles and Facets
        ggplot2::labs(title = paste0("Primer presence on samples: ", PRJ, " project"),
                      subtitle = "Color gradient relative to respective primer count on reads",
                      x = "Primers",
                      y = "Samples") +
        ggplot2::facet_grid(rows = vars(Primer_lbl),
                            cols = vars(Sequences_lbl),
                            scales = "free",
                            space = "free")

      # 4. Save the plot
      ggplot2::ggsave(file = paste0(track_path, "/", 
                                    PRJ, 
                                    "-primers_found_in_reads.pdf"),
                      plot = primers_tile,
                      device = "pdf",
                      width = 10 + (n_primers * 15),
                      height = (n_samples * 1.5) + 3,
                      units = "cm",
                      limitsize = FALSE,
                      dpi = 600)
      
      # 5. Open the plot 
      utils::browseURL(paste0(track_path, "/", PRJ, "-primers_found_in_reads.pdf"))
      }
    ```

    ------------------------------------------------------------------------

-   **Check orientations.** Analyze the generated plots to confirm that primers appear in the expected read files and orientations. The correct interpretation depends on two factors: **how the sequencing library was constructed** (standard vs. mixed orientation) and **whether read-through occurs** (i.e., whether the amplicon is shorter than the read length).

[**Understanding the four orientation columns**]{.underline}

The `allOrients()` function generates four variants of each primer sequence: `Forward` (original sequence), `Complement` (same direction, complementary bases), `Reverse` (original read 3'→5'), and `RevComp` (reverse complement). Only `Forward` and `RevComp` are biologically observable in Illumina sequencing — the polymerase always synthesizes 5'→3', so a primer can only appear at the start of a read in its `Forward` form, or at the end of a read in its `RevComp` form (due to read-through).

**Case 1 — Standard library, amplicon longer than the read length (no read-through).** In a standard Illumina paired-end library, R1 sequences the forward strand 5'→3' (starting from where the FWD primer bound), and R2 sequences the reverse strand 5'→3' (starting from where the REV primer bound). When the amplicon is long enough that neither read reaches the opposite primer, the expected result is:

| Primer  | R1                 | R2                 |
|:--------|:-------------------|:-------------------|
| **FWD** | **Forward** (good) | \~0                |
| **REV** | \~0                | **Forward** (good) |

All other orientation/read combinations should be near zero. *Typical examples:* 16S V3–V4 (\~460 bp) with 2×250 bp reads; 12S V5 with 2×150 bp reads when the amplicon exceeds read length.

**Case 2 — Standard library, amplicon shorter than the read length (read-through occurs).** When the amplicon is shorter than the read length, R1 reads through the entire insert and into the REV primer site, encountering it from the antisense direction — it therefore appears as `RevComp` at the 3' end of R1. Symmetrically, R2 reads through and encounters the FWD primer site as `RevComp` at its 3' end. The expected result is:

| Primer  | R1                                       | R2                                       |
|:----------------|:--------------------------|:--------------------------|
| **FWD** | **Forward** (good, 5' start of R1)       | **RevComp** (read-through, 3' end of R2) |
| **REV** | **RevComp** (read-through, 3' end of R1) | **Forward** (good, 5' start of R2)       |

The `RevComp` read-through signal is not an error — it is expected and **must** be handled by Cutadapt, which trims both the 5' primer and the 3' reverse-complement of the opposite primer from each read. The proportion of reads with read-through signal will vary with the length distribution of the target region: short amplicons will show near-equal counts in `Forward` and `RevComp`, while longer ones will show a weaker `RevComp` signal. *Typical examples:* ITS1/ITS2 fungal barcodes; short COI barcode fragments; short 16S V4 amplicons sequenced with 2×300 bp reads.

**Case 3 — Mixed orientation library (Pre- vs. Post-Normalization).** Some library preparation protocols (e.g., PCR-free workflows, HiSeq/NovaSeq workflows without strand-selection, or pooled multiplexing strategies) ligate adapters randomly. This produces raw sequencing data where approximately half the read pairs have FWD on R1 and the other half have REV on R1. Unprocessed, this generates a roughly equal `Forward` count across both files:

| Primer  | R1                           | R2                           |
|:--------|:-----------------------------|:-----------------------------|
| **FWD** | **Forward** (\~50% of reads) | **Forward** (\~50% of reads) |
| **REV** | **Forward** (\~50% of reads) | **Forward** (\~50% of reads) |

However, if you demultiplexed your data using the `dmx_metabar(mixed_orientation = TRUE)` pipeline, you should **NOT** see this pattern. The `--revcomp` flag passed to Cutadapt automatically detects the inverted reads, physically swaps R1 and R2, and normalizes the read orientation. Consequently, your post-demultiplexing output will successfully mimic a standard library layout (Case 1 or Case 2). If your diagnostic plots *still* display the mixed 50/50 pattern shown above, the normalization step failed or was skipped. DADA2 assumes strict directional uniformity and will fail during the merging step if mixed orientations are provided.

[**Troubleshooting:**]{.underline}

| Pattern observed in the plot                                                                 | Likely cause                                                                                                | Recommended fix                                                                                                                                               |
|:------------------|:---------------------|:------------------------------|
| FWD in R2/**Forward** (strong); REV in R1/**Forward** (strong)                               | R1/R2 file paths are swapped, or FWD/REV primer definitions are swapped in `primersnsamples`                | Swap R1↔R2 path assignments in `sampleidxtbl`, or swap FWD and REV primer entries                                                                             |
| FWD in R1/**RevComp** (strong); REV in R2/**RevComp** (strong); near-zero **Forward** signal | Both primer sequences were entered in reverse-complement direction (e.g., copied from the antisense strand) | Replace both: `FWD <-      FWD.orient[["RevComp"]]` and `REV <- REV.orient[["RevComp"]]`                                                                      |
| REV in R2/**RevComp** instead of R2/**Forward** (FWD signal looks correct)                   | REV primer sequence was entered as its own reverse complement                                               | Replace: `REV <-      REV.orient[["RevComp"]]` before proceeding                                                                                              |
| FWD and REV in both R1/**Forward** and R2/**Forward** in roughly equal proportions           | Mixed orientation library normalization failed or was skipped                                               | Ensure `mixed_orientation = TRUE` was set during demultiplexing so Cutadapt's `--revcomp` normalizes the pairs automatically.                                 |
| No primer detected in any orientation in any file                                            | Wrong primer pair selected; reads are already pre-trimmed; mismatches \> 1; incorrect file paths            | Verify primer sequences against the wet-lab protocol; confirm reads are not pre-trimmed (check FastQC/MultiQC report); increase `max.mismatch` to 2 as a test |
